newsitem.title: UK: Airlines may reassess fuel price management - BP.
newsitem.headline: Airlines may reassess fuel price management - BP.

text.p: Airlines exposed to volatile fluctuations in jet fuel prices may reassess their risk management after a sharp spike last summer, a British Petroleum marketing official said on Monday.

"Prices did spike quite substantially this year so it may cause them to think again and to reassess their position, their risks and what sort of prices they're leaving themselves exposed to," Jason Prior, energy marketing manager at BP Oil International, told Reuters at a swaps conference here.

"Does it always take a disaster to cause people to think again?" he said. "If prices of jet fuel do double and if that is a disaster for that particular company, then we may see more people (using swaps)."
Jet fuel prices rose sharply last summer, gaining over 30 percent in three months and prompting many airlines to add surcharges to their fares.
Prior said most major airlines who have variable costs for jet fuel already use derivatives risk management.
Prior, attending the International Swaps and Derivatives Association conference, said that the first jet fuel swap occurred in 1987 for British Airways.
